props.content: Update 2026-08-03: both production-critical bugs are resolved and verified against the live site. Canonicals, og:url, the 14-route sitemap, and llms.txt all serve https://www.suntiq.ai; JSON-LD ships on every page; the Cloudflare robots.txt injection is gone and every AI crawler is explicitly allowed. The new frontier is agent readiness: isitagentready.com scores suntiq.ai Level 1 of 5 (“Basic Web Presence”), and one robots.txt line — Content Signals — is the whole gate to Level 2. The full ladder is mapped below. Copy: the category SERPs Suntiq should own are still held by thin listicles and booking-software incumbents; nobody in the recreational segment ranks on operational-intelligence language yet.

props.title: Two live bugs bigger than any copy problem
props.subtitle: Both were found live on 2026-07-30 — and both are now FIXED and re-verified against production on 2026-08-03.

props.title: localhost URLs sitewide — FIXED, VERIFIED LIVE
props.content: Every canonical tag, og:url, sitemap entry, and llms.txt link on the live site pointed to http://localhost:3000. Root cause: NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL existed in Vercel production but was an EMPTY string, and the code's `??` fallback doesn't catch empty. RESOLVED: env var set, fallbacks hardened to `||`, deployed 2026-07-31. Verified live 2026-08-03 — canonical, og:url, all 14 sitemap <loc> entries, and every llms.txt link now serve https://www.suntiq.ai.

props.title: Cloudflare AI-crawler block — FIXED, VERIFIED LIVE
props.content: Cloudflare's managed robots.txt was prepending Disallow rules for ClaudeBot, GPTBot, Google-Extended, Amazonbot, and Applebot-Extended above the app's own Allow rules. RESOLVED via the dashboard change: verified 2026-08-03, the live robots.txt now serves ONLY the app's rules — explicit Allow groups for GPTBot, OAI-SearchBot, ChatGPT-User, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot, Google-Extended, GoogleOther, Applebot-Extended, Amazonbot, FacebookBot; only Bytespider stays blocked (our own rule). One residual check: robots.txt is advisory. Cloudflare can also block at the HTTP/WAF layer — confirm in the dashboard that AI Crawl Control lists every crawler as Allow (not Block), the three AI bot policies (Search / Agent / Training) are set to Allow, and AI Labyrinth is off. Those blocks would be invisible in robots.txt.

props.title: Structured data was dead code — FIXED in this pass
props.content: The JsonLd component (Organization + WebSite + breadcrumbs) existed but its only consumer was an orphaned component nothing imports. Zero JSON-LD shipped on any page. RESOLVED: generalized, wired into every public page, deployed — the live homepage now serves two ld+json scripts (verified 2026-08-03).

props.label: Copy findings
props.title: Page-by-page: what to rewrite and why
props.subtitle: Top findings per page with concrete rewrites. Expand what you care about.

props.title: Home (B-) — metadata described a page that doesn't exist
props.content: The old title and description came from the segment config, but HomePage.tsx is fully bespoke and never renders that copy — searchers saw one promise in the SERP and a different headline on arrival. Fixed by the new metadata. Remaining proposals: the advisory-first message (Suntiq advises, you decide) is stated four times — cut to two: hero plus the Trust section. Weave one literal phrase like fleet management for boat clubs into a visible H2 or body line; today operational intelligence carries all the weight and no H1/H2 contains a target phrase.

props.title: Fleet IQ (B) — strongest page, one broken CTA
props.content: Message-match break at the highest-intent click: the hero's secondary CTA reads What operators get but links to #layer, the data-plumbing section; the actual benefits live at #outcomes two sections later. Point it at #outcomes or retitle to How the data flows. Then thread one target phrase per major section without breaking voice — hero lead gets marine fleet management for boat clubs, rental fleets, marinas, and charters; the operating-layer note gets turns raw vessel telematics into one clear operating picture. None of the four target phrases appear in visible copy today.

props.title: Platform (B) — one idea occupying five sections
props.content: The advisory-first / never-silences-a-warning claim is restated near-verbatim five times down the page (promise band, commitments accordion, Judge stage, models section, closing statement). State it once in the promise band; let later sections reference the consequence. Separately, the In the product section is the weakest on the page: Reports at your fingertips is a stock cliché and its lead line is ungrammatical with undefined jargon (real time IQ). Proposed: headline What the fleet console actually shows, lead Readiness sweeps, live vessel state, and maintenance-and-fuel reports — in one screen, wherever you're standing.

props.title: Solutions (C+) — source and live site disagree; zero proof
props.content: Blocking issue first: the checked-out source and the deployed page disagree in three places (CTA copy, mid-page statement band). Confirm which tree shipped before landing any copy edit here. Content-wise this is the highest-intent hub page and it has zero social proof — no customer, no fleet count, no stat. One line fixes it: Piloting now with boat clubs across North America, or name FBC Vancouver if cleared. The live Three names. One system. framing is good — keep whichever wins.

props.title: Situational IQ (B-) — well-crafted, invisible to search
props.content: The word fleet appears only in an image alt attribute — never in a headline or paragraph — despite fleet operators and boat clubs being the named audience. One sentence closes most of the gap: extend the hero line to ...the operational-intelligence layer fleet operators and boat clubs check before every decision. Also replace the two spots where internal shorthand leaks (the clever layers, gateway intelligence layer) with plain language. Research note: real-time vessel situational awareness is the least-competed head term in the whole keyword set — this page can own it.

props.title: Asset IQ (C+) — poetic fragments where keywords should live
props.content: Old title used 18 of 60 characters with zero category terms; the description was a poetic fragment (Wear projected forward, seasons forecast...). Both replaced. Remaining: cut the long-horizon layer of Suntiq from the hero subhead — internal jargon — and work vessel maintenance forecasting or predictive maintenance into visible copy. Research note: borrow the condition-intelligence / maintenance-operating-system framing trending with newer entrants; scope explicitly to boat clubs and fleet operators, not offshore shipping (SpecTec and MariApps own that lane).

props.title: Mechanics (B-) — the free hook was missing from metadata
props.content: The single strongest differentiator — free, no fees, no bidding — wasn't in the title or description a mechanic would search for. Fixed. Remaining: the Standing benefit row is circular (defines standing with standing); proposed rewrite: Completed jobs and owner ratings build your standing. Higher standing means you see new jobs in your area first. And replace all three instances of strategic rollout — a mechanic reads rollout as beta, might get pulled; use free while we onboard the first fleets.

props.title: Partners (B-) — H1 is a near-copy of the Investors page
props.content: A new operational layer for the connected marine ecosystem and the Investors page's The next layer of connected marine intelligence are the same template — abstract platform positioning with nothing partner-specific. The page's best line is buried in the subhead; promote it to the H1: Built with the partners who live with what happens after the sale. Research note: almost no competitor content targets marine OEM telematics integration or dealer/installer partner programs — this page can be category-defining rather than competitive.

props.title: Investors (B-) — fails the 5-second test for cold traffic
props.content: Proposed H1: The operational intelligence layer for modern marine fleets. Proposed subhead: Suntiq turns raw boat telemetry into fleet-wide operational intelligence — for boat clubs, marinas, and the dealers and OEMs behind them. Every proof point on the page is market-level; there is zero company-level traction signal before the NDA gate. One public-safe teaser (in pilot with N boat clubs...) would materially lift gate-request conversion. That number is yours to approve.

props.title: Public sector (C+) — company-voice where value should be
props.content: The hero tells a police dive team what Suntiq is doing internally (Suntiq is evaluating applications...) instead of what they get. Proposed: Suntiq gives public-safety and municipal marine fleets one continuous, plain-language view of vessel readiness — fuel, power, and open issues, before the shift starts. Currently onboarding through private briefings. Research note: this buyer has a wholly separate vendor set (Tidalis, Harbour Systems, Track Star) and vocabulary — compliance, audit trail, multi-agency reporting — do not reuse boat-club language. The page is also not linked from the site nav.

props.title: About (C+) — same three ideas stated twice in a row
props.content: The pull-quote band and the four-card principles grid directly beneath it restate identical ideas (decision support under pressure, in command, safety before spectacle). Let the quote stand as pure atmosphere and let the cards do the explaining. Metadata and canonical fixed in this pass.

props.title: Contact (B-) — the strongest CTA on the page is unreachable
props.content: The Get started tab holds the three-step access flow (sign in, NDA, private room) — the most specific proof-of-process copy on the page — but it is hidden with no visible tab and no link pointing to it; the code comment claiming CallPanel links to #start is stale. Un-hide it or add a hero button Request private access pointing at #start. Also: say under NDA instead of under agreement in the hero so the first mention is as specific as the later ones.

props.title: Terms (B-) and Privacy (C+) — the diligence-audience gap
props.content: Privacy is the real finding: the policy scopes itself to the website only and never mentions vessel location, telemetry, or fleet data — a credibility gap for investors and partners doing data-room diligence on a telemetry company. Proposed additions to Scope and Information-we-collect acknowledging platform data under a separate agreement. Both pages: align date precision (Effective vs Last-updated) and name the actual frameworks (GDPR, CCPA, PIPEDA) instead of depending on where you live.

props.content: Do not chase boat club management software head-on — that term is owned by booking and billing incumbents, and it describes a product Suntiq is not. The winning move on every SERP above is the same: enter with the telemetry-and-decisions story the incumbents structurally cannot tell.

props.label: Competitive landscape
props.title: Four clusters, one real threat
BoatTech.ai — the one to watch
props.content: AI-native, built by a Freedom Boat Club franchisee (135 vessels, FBC Technology Trendsetter of the Year). Same ICP, same AI story. Its own marketing validates the pain points to lead with: reservation availability is the top member complaint, 30%+ dock-staff annual turnover, clubs run on spreadsheets and phone trees. Differentiate on telematics depth, multi-brand fleet support, and price transparency — its pricing page has no public figures.

props.title: Monitoring hardware (Siren, Garmin, BRNKL)
props.content: Siren Marine is Yamaha-owned and ships standard on Helm Master EX. Garmin OnDeck has well-documented user complaints: unlabeled sensor tiles, no alarm acknowledgment, anchor-drag geofence 10x too large, WiFi/cellular handoff friction, MFD integration never shipped. BRNKL is climbing upmarket (NATO study, defense partnerships). All are single-boat, hardware-first — none serve fleet operators. Suntiq's multi-vessel framing is the real differentiator.

props.title: Club and marina SaaS (Dockwa, BoatCloud, Molo, DockMaster)
props.content: Membership, reservations, and billing-first. Almost none foreground telemetry-driven fleet intelligence, maintenance prediction, or real-time asset health. That is the gap Fleet IQ and Asset IQ target — do not compete for their booking keywords.

props.title: What the audience actually talks about (last 30 days)
props.content: 117 items pulled across Reddit, X, TikTok, YouTube, HN. There is no organic conversation about club fleet software — whitespace. What goes viral: fleet-utilization economics (a Tahoe operator's 4-boat, million-dollar-summer thread pulled 2,354 likes) and ownership-pain humor. The line worth stealing from the trade: a boat that is down is a promise you cannot keep to paying members.

props.subtitle: Each is an open lane verified against live search and social data.

props.title: Garmin OnDeck vs Siren Marine page
props.content: Real buyers actively research this exact comparison and both incumbents have specific, documented gaps. A head-to-head page that answers honestly and positions Suntiq for the fleet case captures high-intent traffic neither vendor can.

props.title: Fuel accountability for boat clubs
props.content: Commercial-fleet content quantifies fuel theft at tens of thousands annually; nothing recreational-marine-specific exists. A boat-clubs-lose-X-per-year-to-fuel-discrepancies asset owns the angle before a competitor names it.

props.title: IMO MASS Code thought leadership
props.content: The autonomous/AI-assisted vessel code took effect July 1, 2026 — a fresh, credible regulatory hook for positioning Suntiq's AI as ahead of a real curve. Supporting stat: 65% of maintenance teams plan AI adoption by end of 2026, only 27% are doing it.

props.title: FAQ blocks for AI answer engines
props.content: Question-shaped sections (can I monitor my boat remotely, what is a marine operational intelligence layer) on /platform and the IQ pages. Forum threads currently rank for these — a real answer page outranks a forum post, and FAQ schema makes it citable by AI engines.

props.title: Fleet-utilization economics story
props.content: The proven-viral format in this audience. A club-economics piece (utilization, downtime cost, revenue per boat) built from real telemetry is both content marketing and an investor asset.

Today one dynamic text card (navy, Suntiq, MARINE INTELLIGENCE) serves all 14 routes — and on the live site its URL resolves to localhost, so shares render broken images. Proposed per-page strategy, pending your creative review: keep a repaired global card as the fallback for utility pages; give the home, Fleet IQ, the two IQ pages, mechanics, partners, and investors bespoke 1200x630 cards pairing the page's headline with brand photography from the site's media library. Build them as static exports first (reviewable in Storybook), then wire per-route opengraph-image files.

props.label: Agent readiness
props.title: isitagentready.com scorecard — Level 1 of 5, and the ladder up
props.subtitle: Scanned 2026-08-03 via isitagentready.com (a Cloudflare tool). 21 checks across 5 categories; levels are gated, not point-scored.

props.content: suntiq.ai currently sits at Level 1 — “Basic Web Presence.” Four checks pass: robots.txt, sitemap, explicit AI-bot rules in robots.txt, and — notably — Markdown content negotiation (the site already answers `Accept: text/markdown` with markdown, which most sites fail). Five commerce checks are neutral (not a commerce site) and are excluded from scoring. Everything else fails — but the failures sort cleanly into three tiers: one one-liner that gates Level 2, two cheap discoverability wins, and a deep “agent-native” tier that only makes sense when Suntiq exposes a real API or MCP surface.

props.title: The entire Level 2 gate is one robots.txt line
props.content: The tool's next-level requirement is exactly one item: Content Signals — declared AI-usage preferences in robots.txt, e.g. `Content-Signal: search=yes, ai-input=yes, ai-train=no` (spec: contentsignals.org). Two ways to ship it: add the line to the app's robots.ts (one-line code change, awaiting your approval), or re-enable ONLY the “Display Content Signals Policy” toggle in Cloudflare — which adds signals WITHOUT re-adding the Disallow block. Recommendation: do it in robots.ts so the app owns its whole robots.txt and Cloudflare stays hands-off.

props.title: Cloudflare surface — what to leave alone, what to verify
props.content: Cloudflare has four separate AI-crawler controls, and only one was hurting us. Managed robots.txt (the Disallow injector): now off — keep it off. Still worth a one-time verify in the dashboard: (1) AI Crawl Control — every crawler set to Allow, none on Block/Charge; (2) AI bot policies under Security Settings — Search, Agent, and Training all “Allow (do not block)” — note Cloudflare flips new defaults to block Training + Agent bots on 2026-09-15, so re-check after that date; (3) AI Labyrinth — off. These enforce at the WAF/HTTP layer, so a block there never shows up in robots.txt.

props.title: Cloudflare “AI Search” — checked, not relevant
props.content: developers.cloudflare.com/ai-search is the product formerly called AutoRAG: a managed build-your-own RAG/search backend (index your content into vectors, query via Workers/REST/MCP). It does nothing for being found or cited by ChatGPT, Claude, or Perplexity — it's Algolia-shaped, not GEO-shaped. Only future use: it could power an on-site “ask Suntiq” search or back a Suntiq MCP server — which would incidentally tick the agent-native checks above. Parked.
